hints: Find $f''(x) = \frac{160}{9}(4x-3)^{-1/3}$ and evaluate at each stationary point to determine its nature.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $f(x) = (4x - 3)^{5/3} - \frac{20}{3}x$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$f'(x) = \frac{5}{3}(4x - 3)^{2/3} \cdot 4 - \frac{20}{3} = \frac{20}{3}(4x - 3)^{2/3} - \frac{20}{3}$$

Set the derivative equal to zero to find the stationary points:
$$\frac{20}{3}(4x - 3)^{2/3} = \frac{20}{3} \implies (4x - 3)^{2/3} = 1$$
$$(4x - 3)^2 = 1 \implies 4x - 3 = \pm 1$$
$$4x - 3 = 1 \implies 4x = 4 \implies x = 1$$
$$4x - 3 = -1 \implies 4x = 2 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}$$

Differentiate again to obtain the second derivative:
$$f''(x) = \frac{20}{3} \cdot \frac{2}{3}(4x - 3)^{-1/3} \cdot 4 = \frac{160}{9}(4x - 3)^{-1/3}$$

Evaluate $f''(x)$ at each stationary point:
$$\text{At } x = 1: \quad f''(1) = \frac{160}{9}(1)^{-1/3} = \frac{160}{9} > 0 \implies \text{Minimum at } x = 1$$
$$\text{At } x = \frac{1}{2}: \quad f''(1/2) = \frac{160}{9}(-1)^{-1/3} = -\frac{160}{9} < 0 \implies \text{Maximum at } x = \frac{1}{2}$$

ai_rubric.Second Derivative Test: Evaluates second derivative $\frac{160}{9}(4x-3)^{-1/3}$ to classify $x = \frac{1}{2}$ as a maximum and $x = 1$ as a minimum.

hints: A function is increasing where its derivative $f'(x) > 0$.
Since $f(x)$ has a local maximum at $x = \frac{1}{2}$ and a local minimum at $x = 1$, $f'(x) > 0$ for $x < \frac{1}{2}$ and $x > 1$.
walkthrough:
Set the derivative strictly positive for an increasing function:
$$f'(x) > 0 \implies \frac{20}{3}(4x - 3)^{2/3} - \frac{20}{3} > 0 \implies (4x - 3)^{2/3} > 1$$

State the set of values:
$$x < \frac{1}{2} \quad \text{or} \quad x > 1$$
